page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 architecture. It features AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors offering 192 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 1536.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per core. Network bandwidth reaches a baseline of 600 Gbps, while local storage is absent, requiring external EBS volumes for persistent storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded and memory throughput. The stress-ng multi-core test reached 314,153.46, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, while single-core performance remained average at 1,642.88. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrated 961.55 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 483.73 GB/sec for uncached writes, ranking in the top 10 percent alongside a PassMark memory score of 3,377.92. Cache-level reads scored 21,332.83 GB/sec across its 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache design. Redis SET throughput achieved 362.1 million operations per second, complemented by 47,235.19 operations in PassMark database tests.

The hardware configuration trades single-threaded peak clock speeds for extreme core density, high aggregate memory bandwidth, and 600 Gbps network capacity. In qualitative cost-efficiency terms, the Graviton ARMv9 architecture delivers massive multi-core throughput and high RAM density per compute unit compared to conventional x86 instances, making it cost effective for scale-up in-memory tasks despite the premium scale of a 48xlarge footprint.

The r8gn.48xlarge is suited for massive in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise-scale relational database engines, real-time analytics, and heavy ETL pipelines. Its high network throughput and multi-threaded scaling also support large-scale distributed caching layers and high-volume software compilation clusters.
